canonical.title: Lowest Common Ancestor in a BST
canonical.sourceFilePath: 12. Binary Search Trees/2. Practice Problems/07. LCA in BST.cpp

narrative.title: The Fork Point on the Sorted Routing Tree
narrative.scenario: A packet router organizes destination addresses in a sorted tree, and two packets must share a staging checkpoint on their way to different addresses. The correct checkpoint is the deepest router where the two destinations still travel together: while both targets sit on the same side of a router, the walk continues into that wing; the moment they split — or one of them IS the router — that router is the meeting point.
narrative.inputFormat: A binary search tree as a level-order array (null marks a missing child) plus two integers p and q — the target node values.
narrative.outputFormat: Return the value of the lowest common ancestor of p and q. A node counts as an ancestor of itself.
constraints: All node values are unique; both p and q exist in the tree

testCases.explanation: 2 and 8 split onto opposite wings of 6, making it the fork point.
4 lives under 2, and a node is its own ancestor.

hintLevels: Level 1: Unlike a plain tree, the sorted order tells you which wing each target took — follow the split.
Level 2: Both targets smaller than the node? Go left. Both larger? Go right. Anything else is the answer.
Level 3: The first node where the two targets diverge — or that equals one of them — is the LCA; no post-processing needed.
